llm_summary: The run built a reasonably capable Ironclad deck and reached Act 2, but accumulated substantial HP loss through repeated combats and entered the Automaton fight with only 22 HP. The decisive failure was defensive prioritization in the final combat: at 11 HP with no Block and an attacking Orb, the agent spent the turn mostly attacking instead of securing immediate protection. Earlier card rewards also leaned toward redundant attacks while passing on stronger draw/energy or exhaust-support options.

llm_lessons.title: At critical HP, block before converting energy into damage
llm_lessons.situation: When HP is low, Block is zero, and at least one enemy is attacking, especially if another enemy is not applying immediate pressure.
llm_lessons.lesson: Treat survival as the primary objective: play a legal defensive card such as True Grit+ before making marginal attacks. Do not spend the whole turn attacking an enemy that is already low unless the attack immediately prevents more damage than the available block would.
evidence_points: On Turn 5 of the Automaton fight, the player had 11/80 HP, 0 Block, 4 Energy, and an Orb at 40 HP with Intent ATTACK; True Grit+ was a legal alternative.
The chosen sequence played Dark Shackles and several attacks, ended the turn with 0 Block, and left the Orb alive at 13 HP.
On the next turn, the player again began at only 10/80 HP while both the Automaton and Orb had Intent ATTACK.
llm_lessons.reasoning: The logged state shows an immediate survival problem and a legal defensive option, while the chosen attacks did not kill the attacking Orb until the following turn. This pattern left almost no margin for the next enemy attack and is more causally relevant than simply blaming the eventual death.

llm_lessons.title: Stop adding redundant attacks once the attack package is established
llm_lessons.situation: After several attack rewards have already been taken, especially when the deck still needs draw, energy, or exhaust support.
llm_lessons.lesson: Prefer cards that improve consistency or support the existing engine over another merely adequate attack. In particular, reassess repeated attack rewards and favor options like Offering or Feel No Pain when they directly address energy, draw, or exhaust synergies.
evidence_points: The run took Pommel Strike at Act 1 Floors 10, 11, and 12; the final 31-card deck contains three Pommel Strikes.
At Act 1 Floor 13, Offering was available but Shrug It Off was chosen; at Floor 14, Feel No Pain was available but Headbutt was chosen.
The final deck contains Fiend Fire+, True Grit+, True Grit, and Warcry, so exhaust and hand-quality support were relevant to the eventual build.
llm_lessons.reasoning: The final deck confirms that the repeated Pommel rewards were permanent additions, not generated cards, and that the deck already had substantial attack density. The skipped Offering and Feel No Pain represented opportunities to improve energy/draw or exploit the deck's exhaust cards rather than further increasing redundant attacks.

human_feedback: Manage block and attacks better during combats, try to minimise hp taken as much as possible

interventions.note: Offering is always a good card to take over any other option
